agenda_text:
City Council of Monterey Park
  The City Council Acting on Behalf of the Successor Agency of the Former Redevelopment
 Agency, the Housing Authority, the Monterey Park Financing Authority and the Monterey Park
  Geologic Hazard Abatement District Agenda

  Regular Meeting - Amended to add Item No. 9A - Requires 4/5 vote to add
  Monterey Park City Hall Council Chambers
  320 West Newmark Avenue, Monterey Park, CA 91754

  Wednesday, May 20, 2026
  6:30 PM
  Mission Statement
The mission of the City of Monterey Park is to provide excellent service, foster growth and opportunity,
  and create a joyous and collaborative environment.
  Land Acknowledgment
We would like to acknowledge that the land we inhabit today was once known as Tovangaar, the home
 of the Gabrieleño-Tongva people. We show our respect to the Gabrieleño-Tongva people, as well as
  all Indigenous people, past, present, and future, and honor their labor as original caretakers of this
land. We commit to uplifting the Gabrieleño-Tongva people, invite you to acknowledge the history, and
  join us in caring for this land.

General Information
Documents related to an Agenda item are available to the public in the City Clerk’s Office located at
320 West Newmark Avenue, Monterey Park, CA 91754, during normal business hours and
at www.montereypark.ca.gov/agendas.

The public may watch the meeting live on the city’s cable channel MPKTV (AT&T U-verse, channel 99
or Charter Communications, channel 182) or by visiting the city’s website at
http://www.montereypark.ca.gov/133/City-Council-Meeting-Videos. Per the Americans with Disabilities
Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please email City Hall
at mpclerk@montereypark.ca.gov or call (626) 307-1359 for reasonable accommodation at least 48
hours before a meeting. Council Chambers are wheelchair accessible.

Public Comment for Matters Not on the Agenda
Pursuant to Rule 5 of Resolution No. 12226 (adopted February 17, 2021), speakers are limited to a
total of five minutes for Public Comment and a total of five minutes on all other items on the Agenda.
 Exception - See Public Hearing Procedures under Rule 7, Resolution No. 12226. If desirable, the
Mayor and City Council may change the amount of time allowed for speakers.

While all comments are welcome, the Brown Act does not allow the City Council to take action on any
item not on the agenda. The Council may briefly respond to comments after Public Communications is
closed. Persons may speak to any matter that is not on the Agenda but within the City Council's
subject-matter jurisdiction at this time. Comments regarding an Agenda item, including the Consent
 Calendar, will be heard when that matter is called. Written Communication is accepted up to 24 hours
before the meeting by completing an online form at www.montereypark.ca.gov/writtencomm. Written
communications are provided to the City Council.

Live Translation:
Meetings will be translated (transcribed or audio) to the language you select. Instructions are provided
below.

Las reuniones se traducirán (por escrito o por audio) al idioma que seleccione. Las instrucciones se
encuentran a continuación.

1.  Call to Order
  Mayor

2.  Flag Salute
  The Monterey Park Police Explorers

3.  Roll Call
  Henry Lo, Vinh Ngo, Jose Sanchez, Thomas Wong, Elizabeth Yang

4.  Telecommunications Announcement, if requested

5.  Agenda Revisions and Additions
 6.  Presentation

  6.A. San Gabriel Valley Mosquito and Vector Control District

  6.B. City Wide Communications Survey Results

  6.C. Development Projects Update — Community Development Department

7.  Public Comments

8.  Staff Communications

  8.A. Police Department

  8.B. Fire Department

  8.C. Recreation & Community Services Department

9.  Old Business

  9.A. [REQUIRES 4/5 VOTE TO ADD] Adopt a Resolution Authorizing the Sale of Real
  Property Located at 2537-2543 Lee Avenue, South El Monte, as Partial Satisfaction of
  Debt Owed to the City for Nuisance Abatement Costs Associated with 1688 West
  Garvey Avenue.

  It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Add this matter to the Regular Agenda as Item No. 9A upon a 4/5 vote pursuant to
  Government Code § 54954.2(b)(2) because (a) there is a need to take immediate
  action and (b) that the need for action came to the City’s attention after the Regular
  Agenda was posted;
  2. Adopting a Resolution authorizing the sale of real property commonly known as
  2537-2543 Lee Avenue, South El Monte, California, APNs 5281-012-011 and 5281-
  012-012, in partial satisfaction of debt owed to the City by Center Intl Investments,
  LLC (“CII”) related to the City’s nuisance abatement of the GAP Property located at
  1688 West Garvey Avenue;
  3. Authorizing the City Manager, or designee, to take all actions necessary to effectuate
  the marketing and sale of the South El Monte property, on terms approved as to form
  by the City Attorney; and
  4. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

  CEQA (California Environmental Quality Act):
  The City reviewed the environmental impacts of the proposed Ordinance pursuant to the
  California Environmental Quality Act (Public Resources Code §§ 21000, et seq. “CEQA”)
  and the regulations promulgated thereunder (14 Cal. Code of Regs. §§ 15000, et seq., the
  “CEQA Guidelines”). This activity is exempt from the CEQA pursuant to CEQA Guidelines §
  15601(b)(3) as it contemplates only administrative actions related to the acquisition of real
  property and it can be seen with certainty that there is no possibility that it may have a
  significant effect on the environment.

10. Consent Calendar
  All items under the Consent Calendar are considered by the City Council to be routine and will be
  enacted by one motion. Specific items may be removed from the Consent Calendar at the request
 of any member of the City Council for separate consideration.

10.A. Tree Memorial Program Recommendation for Shirley Hwong and Fumiko "Mickey"
  Maruya

  It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Authorizing the City Manager to take actions to honor Shirley Hwong with a memorial
  tree and plaque;
  2. Authorizing the City Manager to take actions to honor Fumiko “Mickey” Maruya with
  a memorial tree and plaque; and
  3. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

10.B. Third Amendment to Agreement with HDL Coren & Cone for Property Tax
  Consultation Services

  It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Authorizing the City Manager to execute a third amendment to HDL Coren & Cone
  Agreement No. 1975-A in a form approved by the City Attorney to continue providing
  property tax consultation services from July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2031, for an
  additional amount of $130,000, increasing the total contract amount to a not-to-
  exceed amount of $283,250 for the full Agreement term; and
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

10.C. Amendment to License Agreement with the Friends of the Monterey Park Library, Inc.
  for Use of Library Bookstore

  It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Authorizing the City Manager, or designee, to execute an amendment to the license
  Agreement No. 2533-A with the Friends of the Monterey Park Library, Inc. to transfer
  rights and responsibilities to the Monterey Park Library Foundation for space within
  the Bruggemeyer Library to sell used books; and
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

10.D. Amendment agreement with Commercial Door for Continued Commercial-Grade Door
  and Gate Maintenance

  It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Authorizing the City Manager to execute a Second Amendment to Agreement 2440-
  A with Commercial Door of Los Angeles County, Inc., in a form approved by the City
  Attorney, to increase compensation and extend the term for continued commercial-
  grade door and gate maintenance; and
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

10.E. Amendment to Agreement No. 2477-A with Tripepi Smith & Associates, Inc.

  It is recommended that the City Council consider:
   1. Authorizing the City Manager to execute a first amendment to agreement no. 2477-A
  with Tripepi Smith & Associates, Inc., in a form approved by the City Attorney, to
  provide marketing and public affairs consulting services through June 30, 2027; and
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

  10.F. Resolution Amending Resolution No. 10485 to Update the Composition of the
  Nomination Committee for the Tree Memorial Nomination and Award Program

  It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Amending Resolution No. 10485, to update the composition for the Nomination
  Committee for the Tree Memorial Nomination and Award Program to include
  members of the Community Participation Commission, Recreation and Parks
  Commission, and Aging Commission; and
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

11. Public Hearing

  11.A. Public Hearing to receive comments on the Program Year 2026-2027 Annual Action
  Plan for the Community Development Block Grant and HOME Investment
  Partnerships Programs

  It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Opening the public hearing to receive citizen input on community needs and priorities
  prior to final Community Development Block Grant and HOME funding decisions for
  the Program Year 2026-2027 Annual Action Plan; and

  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

12. New Business

  12.A. Establish a Temporary Ad Hoc Subcommittee to Explore Funding Strategies for the
  Barnes Park Aquatic Center

  It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Establishing a temporary Ad Hoc Subcommittee to assist staff in exploring funding
  opportunities and strategic partnerships for the proposed Barnes Park Aquatic
  Center;
  2. Appointing up to two (2) City Councilmembers to serve on the Ad Hoc
  Subcommittee;
  3. Appointing Council Member Thomas Wong to serve on the Ad Hoc Subcommittee;
  4. Providing direction regarding funding strategies, partnership opportunities, and
  priorities to be explored by the Ad Hoc Subcommittee; and
  5. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

13. City Communications (City Council) / Future Agenda Items

14. Closed Session (if Required; City Attorney to Announce)
 15. Adjournment

  Minutes
  Monterey Park City Council
  Financing Authority (MPFA)
  Housing Authority (MPHA)
  Geologic Hazard Abatement District (GHAD)
  Successor Agency (SA)
  Regular Meeting
  May 20, 2026
The City Council, the Financing Authority (MPFA), the Housing Authority (MPHA), the
Geologic Hazard Abatement District (GHAD), and the Successor Agency (SA) of the
City of Monterey Park held a Regular Meeting of the Council in the Council Chamber,
located at 320 West Newmark Avenue in the City of Monterey Park, Wednesday, May
20, 2026, at 6:30 p.m.

1.  Call to Order
  Mayor Yang called the meeting to order at 6:38 p.m.

2.  Flag Salute
  The Monterey Park Police Explorers led the flag salute.

3.  Roll Call
  City Clerk Maychelle Yee called the roll:

  Council Members Present: Henry Lo, Vinh Ngo, Jose Sanchez, Thomas Wong,
  Elizabeth Yang
  Council Members Absent: None

  Also present:
  City Treasurer Amy Lee
  City Manager Inez Alvarez
  City Attorney Karl Berger
  Assistant City Manager Diana Garcia
  Director of Finance Martha Garcia
  Director of Human Resources and Risk Management Christine Tomikawa
  Director of Community Development Timothy Hou
  Director of Recreation and Community Services Robert Aguirre
  City Librarian Kristin Olivarez
  Director of Public Works Shawn Igoe
  Police Chief Scott Wiese
  Fire Chief Jason Hing
  Deputy Fire Chief Ryan Weddle
  Finance Manager Laura Borjon
  Economic Development Manager Joseph Torres

  Mission Statement
 The mission of the City of Monterey Park is to provide excellent service, foster growth
  and opportunity, and create a joyous and collaborative environment
   74-212
  May 20, 2026

  Recreation and Community Services Manager Christina Alatorre
  IT Manager Martin Dinh
  Principal Management Analyst Rebecca Bojorquez
  Principal Management Analyst Michelle Marquez
  Administrative Aid Anays Navarro
  City Communications Fellow Citlali Tejeda
  Deputy City Clerk Cindy Trang
  Office Assistant Michelle Martinez

  Virtually present:
  None.

4.  Telecommunications Announcement, if requested
  None.

5.  Agenda Revisions and Additions
  City Manager Alvarez announced the addition of Agenda Item No. 9.A. requiring a
  4/5 vote to add the item to the agenda. She requested to have Agenda Item No.
  10.B. tabled for the next regular City Council meeting.

  Mayor Yang requested to have Public Comments be heard before Agenda Item
  Nos. 6.B. and 6.C.

  Action Taken: The City Council approved the addition of Agenda Item No. 9.A. to
  the agenda through a required 4/5 vote.

  Motion: Moved by Mayor Pro Tem Lo and seconded by Council Member Wong,
  motion carried by the following vote:

  Ayes: Council Members: Henry Lo, Vinh Ngo, Jose Sanchez, Thomas Wong,
  Elizabeth Yang
  Noes: Council Members: None
  Absent: Council Members: None
  Abstain: Council Members: None
  Recusal: Council Members: None

6.  Presentation

  6.A. San Gabriel Valley Mosquito and Vector Control District
  Joseph Leon presented Anais Medina Diaz, Director of Communications of
  the San Gabriel Valley Mosquito Vector Control District (SGV MVCD). Director
  of Communications Diaz exhibited a PowerPoint presentation about SGV
  MVCD's mission and the services they provide to the cities in the San Gabriel
  Valley (SGV), such as surveillance, larval control operations, communications
  and emergency response services. She provided context about the West Nile
  Virus, its detection and treatment process.
   74-213
  May 20, 2026

  6.B. City Wide Communications Survey Results
  This Agenda Item was heard after Public Communications.

  Assistant City Manager Garcia introduced City Communication Fellow Tejeda.
  City Communication Fellow Tejeda shared a PowerPoint presentation
  explaining her role in expanding and refining the City's outreach efforts to
  enhance communication between the City and its residents. She provided an
  overview of the survey, shared its key findings and expressed future goals to
  develop strategies to engage the residents with content through different
  channels of communication.

  6.C. Development Projects Update — Community Development Department
  This Agenda Item was heard after Agenda Item No. 6.B.

  Economic Development Manager Torres presented a PowerPoint
  presentation on updates regarding current and upcoming developments in the
  City. He elaborated on (1) completed projects, such as the new Starbucks
  Drive-through and Varsity Jujitsu School; (2) projects nearing completion,
  which encompass Whitmore Villas, the East Garvey Ave retail market, and the
  façade renovation on Lincoln Center; (3) projects under construction, such as
  the A-1 self-storage facility, Thumbling Dumpling restaurant, and the
  renovations on 601 W. Garvey Ave; and (4) projects with issued permits,
  which include the senior housing project on 188 S. Chandler Ave., the mixed-
  use project on 114 E. Garvey Ave., the multifamily housing project on Hellman
  Ave., a mixed-use project in Deerfield Plaza, a mixed-use project on 122 W
  Garvey Ave., town home developments on 507 Chandler Ave, and a mixed-
  use project on 808 W. Garvey Ave.

  He welcomed new businesses in the city, which included La Diosa de Los
  Moles, Asayoru Maid Café, Yihui Coffee, ReeWorkMe Fitness Center and
  Swank Salon, and introduced upcoming businesses expected to open in
  Monterey Park, such as The Melt and Da Vien Coffee.

7.  Public Comments
  Public Comments were heard after Agenda Item No. 6.A.

  • Randye Kay expressed her concerns regarding the potential increase in
  traffic and noise disruption a proposed multifamily housing project on
  Hellman Ave will bring to the residents in the surrounding area and
  recommended it be moved to Saturn Park.

  • Dori Ho, an Alhambra resident, shared her opposition towards a proposed
  multifamily housing project on Hellman Ave and elaborated on the current
  traffic issues Hellman Ave is experiencing.
   74-214
  May 20, 2026

  • Caleb Kwok voiced his opposition regarding a proposed multifamily housing
  project on Hellman Ave, claiming the project will not only affect Monterey
  Park but also nearby cities as well.

  • Dawn Rock commented on the City's opportunity to secure funding and
  temporary infrastructure for the Barnes Park Aquatic Center during the
  2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

  • Martha expressed her frustrations regarding the proposed multifamily
  housing project on Hellman Ave and shared her opinion on the lack of
  parking during the So Cal Card conventions hosted by Courtyard Marriott.

  • Bruce Mok shared his lifelong residency in the San Gabriel Valley and
  articulated his frustrations about the potential increase in traffic and noise a
  new proposed multifamily housing project would bring to the neighborhood.
  He requested to have the project be moved elsewhere or reduce the
  number of units to facilitate traffic issues.

  • Nancy Nguyen talked about the zoning change implemented on Vagabond
  Drive that has since changed from residential to commercial, commented
  on her recent meeting with Community Development Director Hou and City
  Manager Alvarez regarding ways to change the zoning back to residential
  and requested assistance from city staff to help achieve it.

  • Paul Lam reported an overpopulation on Hathaway St. and Hellman Ave,
  especially during school hours, and claimed the area is dangerous to walk
  on due to the number of traffic accidents that occur.

  • The City Clerk’s office received and filed a written communication from
  Noya Wang, City Council Member from the City of Alhambra speaking on
  behalf of her constituents, conveyed their concerns regarding the proposed
  multifamily housing project on Hellman Ave.

8.  Staff Communications

  8.A. Police Department
  Police Chief Wiese exhibited a PowerPoint presentation detailing the
  Neighborhood Watch Program with the five districts in the City and
  recommended residents to join the program. He shared the department's
  monthly statistics regarding crime and talked about the National Incident
  Based Reporting System (NIBRS) the Federal Bureau of Investigation's
  platform for tracking and reporting crime data in the United States.
   74-215
  May 20, 2026

  8.B. Fire Department
  Deputy Fire Chief Weddle presented a PowerPoint presentation highlighting
  the upcoming Sidewalk CPR event on Saturday, June 6, 2026, meant to
  educate the community on how to recognize cardiac arrest, call 911 and to
  perform high-quality chest compressions.

  8.C. Recreation & Community Services Department
  Director of Recreation and Community Services Aguirre depicted a
  PowerPoint presentation thanking the residents for attending the Play Days
  event and introduced upcoming activities, which include the Unspoken
  Conversations event, the Memorial Day Ceremony at the American Legion,
  the Monterey Park Health Fair at the Langley Center, the San Gabriel Valley
  Pride Parade and Festival, Let's Kick-It Soccer Clinic and Watch Party and the
  Independence Day Celebration. He introduced the brand-new pilot program
  with Dial a Ride and MPK Transit, to expand transportation services to seniors
  in the City.

9.  Old Business

  9.A. [REQUIRES 4/5 VOTE TO ADD] Adopt a Resolution Authorizing the Sale
  of Real Property Located at 2537-2543 Lee Avenue, South El Monte, as
  Partial Satisfaction of Debt Owed to the City for Nuisance Abatement
  Costs Associated with 1688 West Garvey Avenue.
  The history regarding the City’s nuisance abatement efforts at 1688 West
  Garvey Avenue (the GAP) are well documented. A more complete
  background may be reviewed online
  (https://www.montereypark.ca.gov/1409/1688-West-Garvey-Avenue).

  The Lee Avenue property in South El Monte was one of two parcels that
  provided security for CII’s obligations tied to nuisance abatement at 1688
  West Garvey Avenue, and the City accepted title to that property in April 2025
  as partial satisfaction of the outstanding debt. In late 2025, the City entered
  escrow with tenants on Lee Avenue. Regrettably, the tenants were unable to
  secure title insurance for the transaction. On May 19, 2026 (yesterday), the
  City was informed that title insurance would be issued; the City’s broker
  requested immediate action to verify the City Manager’s signature authority for
  the sale of this property so that escrow may close next week. Adopting the
  proposed Resolution will ensure timely closing of escrow and recovery of
  $2.5M in debt owed to the City by CII.
   74-216
  May 20, 2026

CEQA (California Environmental Quality Act):
The City reviewed the environmental impacts of the proposed Ordinance
pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (Public Resources Code
§§ 21000, et seq. “CEQA”) and the regulations promulgated thereunder (14
Cal. Code of Regs. §§ 15000, et seq., the “CEQA Guidelines”). This activity is
exempt from the CEQA pursuant to CEQA Guidelines § 15601(b)(3) as it
contemplates only administrative actions related to the acquisition of real
property and it can be seen with certainty that there is no possibility that it may
have a significant effect on the environment.

Recommendations:
It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Add this matter to the Regular Agenda as Item No. 9A upon a 4/5 vote
  pursuant to Government Code § 54954.2(b)(2) because (a) there is a
  need to take immediate action and (b) that the need for action came to
  the City’s attention after the Regular Agenda was posted;
  2. Adopting a Resolution authorizing the sale of real property commonly
  known as 2537-2543 Lee Avenue, South El Monte, California, APNs
  5281-012-011 and 5281-012-012, in partial satisfaction of debt owed to
  the City by Center Intl Investments, LLC (“CII”) related to the City’s
  nuisance abatement of the GAP Property located at 1688 West Garvey
  Avenue;
  3. Authorizing the City Manager, or designee, to take all actions
  necessary to effectuate the marketing and sale of the South El Monte
  property, on terms approved as to form by the City Attorney; and
  4. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

Discussion: City Attorney Berger presented a staff report regarding the
proposed resolution to authorize the sale of real property commonly known as
2537-2543 Lee Avenue, South El Monte, California in partial satisfaction of
debt owed to the City by Center Intl Investments, LLC.

Action Taken: The City Council approved the recommendations and
approved and adopted Resolution No. 2026-R37.

Motion: Moved by Council Member Sanchez and seconded by Mayor Pro
Tem Lo, motion carried by the following vote:

Ayes: Council Members: Henry Lo, Vinh Ngo, Jose Sanchez, Thomas Wong,
Elizabeth Yang
Noes: Council Members: None
Absent: Council Members: None
Abstain: Council Members: None
Recusal: Council Members: None
   74-217
  May 20, 2026

  Resolution No. 2026-R37
  A Resolution authorizing the City Manager to execute a purchase and sale
  agreement between the buyer identified in escrow and the City of Monterey
  Park for the disposition of real property located at 2537-2543 Lee Avenue,
  South El Monte, California, commonly identified as APNS 5281-012-011 and
  5281-012-012 (currently APNS 5281-012-270 and 5281-012-271)

10. Consent Calendar
  All items under the Consent Calendar are considered by the City Council to be
  routine and will be enacted by one motion. Specific items may be removed from
  the Consent Calendar at the request of any member of the City Council for
  separate consideration.

  Action Taken: The City Council approved Agenda Item Nos. 10.A., 10.C., 10.D.,
  10.E. and 10.F. reading resolutions and ordinances by the title only and waiving
  further reading thereof. Agenda Item No. 10.B. was tabled for the next Regular
  City Council meeting and was not heard for discussion.

  Motion: Moved by Council Member Sanchez and seconded by Council Member
  Wong, motion carried by the following vote:

  Ayes: Council Members: Henry Lo, Vinh Ngo, Jose Sanchez, Thomas Wong,
  Elizabeth Yang
  Noes: Council Members: None
  Absent: Council Members: None
  Abstain: Council Members: None
  Recusal: Council Members: None

  10.A. Tree Memorial Program Recommendation for Shirley Hwong and
  Fumiko "Mickey" Maruya
  Nominations for the Tree Memorial Recognition Program were advertised and
  accepted in February 2026. The Recreation and Community Services
  Department received nomination applications for both Shirley Hwong and
  Fumiko “Mickey” Maruya.

  Subsequently, the Tree Memorial Program Ad-hoc Committee, consisting of
  three Community Participation Commissioners and two Recreation and Parks
  Commissioners, met to review the nominations and discuss their
  consideration for a Tree Memorial based on the criteria established in
  Resolution Nos.10485 and 11484 (Attachment 1 to the staff report).
   74-218
  May 20, 2026

  The Committee reviewed all the nomination applications and associated
  documents Shirley Hwong and Fumiko “Mickey” Maruya (Attachment 2 to the
  staff report). The committee voted unanimously to recommend that the City
  Council approve honoring Fumiko “Mickey” Maruya and Shirley Hwong with a
  Tree Memorial for their service and positive impact on the Monterey Park
  Community.

  Recommendations:
  It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Authorizing the City Manager to take actions to honor Shirley Hwong
  with a memorial tree and plaque;
  2. Authorizing the City Manager to take actions to honor Fumiko “Mickey”
  Maruya with a memorial tree and plaque; and
  3. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

  Action Taken: The City Council approved the recommendations, on Consent
  Calendar.

10.B Third Amendment to Agreement with HDL Coren & Cone for Property
  Tax Consultation Services
  On July 1, 2016, the City entered into a 5-year Services Agreement with HDL
  Coren & Cone for property tax consultation services for a term from July 1,
  2016, to June 30, 2021, for $18,250. On November 2, 2016, the City
  executed a first amendment to add services and increase compensation to
  $28,250. On June 16, 2021, City Council approved a second amendment to
  extend the term to June 30, 2026 and increase the contract amount to
  $153,250.

  It is recommended that Council authorize the City Manager to execute a Third
  Amendment to the HDL Coren & Cone Agreement No. 1975-A for continued
  Property Tax Consulting Services from July 1, 2026, to June 30, 2031, for an
  additional $130,000, increasing the total contract amount to an amount not-
  to-exceed $283,250.

  Recommendations:
  It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Authorizing the City Manager to execute a third amendment to HDL
  Coren & Cone Agreement No. 1975-A in a form approved by the City
  Attorney to continue providing property tax consultation services from
  July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2031, for an additional amount of
  $130,000, increasing the total contract amount to a not-to-exceed
  amount of $283,250 for the full Agreement term; and
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.
   74-219
  May 20, 2026

  Action Taken: During Agenda Revisions and Deletions, the item was tabled
  for the next Regular City Council meeting and was not heard for
  consideration.
10.C. Amendment to License Agreement with the Friends of the Monterey
  Park Library, Inc. for Use of Library Bookstore
  On February 19, 2026, the City executed a license agreement with the
  Friends of the Monterey Park Library, Inc., a California public benefit
  corporation, (the “Friends”) to utilize space within the Bruggemeyer Library
  (the “Library”) to operate a volunteer-run bookstore. At their meeting on April
  10, 2026, the Friends voted to dissolve the organization. Hence, they will no
  longer operate the Friends Bookstore in the Library.

  The Monterey Park Library Foundation, a nonprofit 501(c)3 organization, (the
  “Foundation”) will take over operation of the bookstore. Through the sale of
  used book donations, the Foundation will raise funds to support the activities
  of the Library, such as children’s performers, reading program incentives, and
  library branded giveaways for distribution at outreach events.

  The City would like to amend the existing license agreement to transfer and
  assign rights and responsibilities for the bookstore from the Friends to the
  Foundation. Under the amendment, the City would provide space for the
  Foundation to continue the bookstore’s practice of selling donated books.

  The Foundation must maintain active status and good standing as a non-
  profit organization; manage the operations of the bookstore; and use all
  proceeds generated by the bookstore to support Library programs and
  services.

  Recommendations:
  It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Authorizing the City Manager, or designee, to execute an amendment
  to the license Agreement No. 2533-A with the Friends of the Monterey
  Park Library, Inc. to transfer rights and responsibilities to the Monterey
  Park Library Foundation for space within the Bruggemeyer Library to
  sell used books; and
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

  Action Taken: The City Council approved the recommendation, on Consent
  Calendar.
   74-220
  May 20, 2026

10.D. Amendment agreement with Commercial Door for Continued
  Commercial-Grade Door and Gate Maintenance
  Commercial Door of Los Angeles County, Inc. (“Commercial Door”) currently
  provides commercial-grade door and gate maintenance services across all
  City-owned facilities. It is recommended the City Council approve a Second
  Amendment with Commercial Door to increase the total contract amount to
  $150,000 through June 30, 2027.
  Recommendations:
  It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Authorizing the City Manager to execute a Second Amendment to
  Agreement 2440-A with Commercial Door of Los Angeles County, Inc.,
  in a form approved by the City Attorney, to increase compensation and
  extend the term for continued commercial-grade door and gate
  maintenance; and
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

12. New Business

  12.A. Establish a Temporary Ad Hoc Subcommittee to Explore Funding
  Strategies for the Barnes Park Aquatic Center
  The City is currently exploring opportunities to fund and construct the
  proposed Barnes Park Aquatic Center, and staff seeks City Council direction
  and collaboration to identify viable funding mechanisms and strategic
  partnerships to support a successful project. In order to facilitate focused
  discussions and coordination, staff recommends establishing an Ad Hoc
  Subcommittee composed of up to two City Council members. Council
  Member Thomas Wong has offered to serve on the subcommittee and City
  Council may consider appointing one other Council Member if desired.
   74-223
  May 20, 2026

The Ad Hoc Subcommittee would work with staff to evaluate potential funding
opportunities, provide strategic guidance, and support outreach efforts related
to the project. Funding opportunities and strategies may include grants, public
and private partnerships, sponsorships, and alternative funding mechanisms.
The Subcommittee would also work to identify community partners that may
be able to support the project.

The Ad Hoc Subcommittee would serve in an advisory capacity, providing
feedback and recommendations to staff as well as providing updates to the
City Council. Meetings would be scheduled on an as-needed and may be
held on various days and at various times. The Subcommittee would dissolve
upon completion of its assigned purpose.

Recommendations:
It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Establishing a temporary Ad Hoc Subcommittee to assist staff in
  exploring funding opportunities and strategic partnerships for the
  proposed Barnes Park Aquatic Center;
  2. Appointing up to two (2) City Council members to serve on the Ad Hoc
  Subcommittee;
  3. Appointing Council Member Thomas Wong to serve on the Ad Hoc
  Subcommittee;
  4. Providing direction regarding funding strategies, partnership
  opportunities, and priorities to be explored by the Ad Hoc
  Subcommittee; and
  5. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

Discussion: Director of Recreation and Community Services Aguirre shared
a staff report regarding the potential exploration of funding opportunities for
the Barnes Park Aquatic Center.

Action Taken: The City Council approved the recommendations and
appointed Council Member Wong and Mayor Pro Tem Lo to serve on the Ad
Hoc Subcommittee.
